s0CADF6.name: Ending enemy scene: set up and slide layers
summary: Two routines for the ending enemy parade ([$1DE9] = scene 0 Lakitu ... 12 Bowser). $0CADF6 (JSL from game mode $23) uploads the scene's enemy-name screen image
(ImagePointers entry 72 + scene), appends an extra image when [$1EEB] bit 7 is set (post-Special World flag), sets the window HDMA band split
($04A0/$04AA/$04B4 entries 2 and 3 = DATA_0CADB5[scene] and $88 minus that) and Layer 2 Y from DATA_0CADC2, starts the layers off-screen and sets [$145B] = $FF hold time.
$0CAEAD (JSR from CODE_0C93A5, game mode $25) runs each frame: Layer 1/3 move right 2 px, the opposite-moving mirror ($1462/$146A) left 2 px, Layer 2 at 1 px; they pause

for [$145B] frames when they meet at 0, then slide out; then the game mode advances ($26 for Bowser, else $22 to fade to the next enemy). Bowser (scene 12) does not slide, it just waits. Ends by jumping to CODE_0CB5BC.

s0CAF11.name: Ending scene background sprite lists
summary: 13 FF-terminated lists (one per ending enemy scene) of 4-byte entries: X, Y, tile, properties. DATA_0CB5A2 gives each scene's list offset from $0CAF11.
Properties: bit 7/6 = flips, bits 3-1 = palette, bit 0 = name table, bit 4 = large (16x16) size, bit 5 = scroll with [$1462] instead of [$1A].
Bits 4 and 5 are replaced by the priority bits when drawn (see CODE_0CB5BC). Rows below show 's<scene>: x y tile prop' for entries starting in the row.

s0CB5A2.name: Table: scene sprite list offsets
summary: 13 words, one per ending enemy scene: offset of that scene's sprite list from $0CAF11. Lists are not stored in scene order.

s0CB5BC.name: Draw ending scene background sprites
summary: Builds extended OAM from the current scene's list in DATA_0CAF11 (offset from DATA_0CB5A2[[$1DE9]]), filling slots 127 downwards until an X of $FF.
Each sprite's X is reduced by the layer scroll ([$1A], or [$1462] if properties bit 5 is set); X bit 8 and the size bit go into the high table at $0420+slot.
Priority bits come from [$00]: $20, or $30 for scene 5.

s0CB636.name: Screen image: THE END
summary: Two 12-tile rows at VRAM $50EA and $510A (Layer 3): 'T H E   E N D' as tops (tiles $Cx/$E3) and bottoms (+$10), with tile $FC as the spaces.
Screen image format (read by LoadScrnImage, $0085D2): blocks of VRAM word address (high, low), flags/length high (bit 7 = write down a column,
bit 6 = RLE, bits 5-0 = length high), length low; length = byte count - 1. Then tile/attribute byte pairs, or for RLE one tile and one attribute that are repeated. A $FF byte ends the image.
Followed by $FF padding up to $0CB7FF.

s0CB800.name: Screen image: cutscene 4 background
summary: Background tilemap for cutscene 4 (Ludwig), ImagePointers entry 5 (chosen through DATA_009460 in bank 00).
Clears VRAM $3000+ with tile $FA, paints rows of tile $F8 (47-tile runs from $3064 down) and then single tiles (e.g. $B6, $F1) and ground rows at $31E4/$3204 (tiles $8A, $9A).

s0CB9BF.name: Screen image: cutscene castle picture
summary: ImagePointers entry 69, the second image loaded for every cutscene ($CF in CODE_0094BF). Clears VRAM $2000+ with tile $F8, then draws a 6x9 tile picture
(nine 6-tile rows from $20F4, 32 words apart), probably the castle; its palette comes from CutsceneCastlePal.

s0CBA56.name: Screen image: cutscene 3 and 7 background
summary: ImagePointers entry 67 (bank 00 comment: cutscene border, cave ground), used by cutscenes 3 (Lemmy) and 7 (Larry).
Clears VRAM $3000+ with tile $FA, fills 12 rows with tile $FA, then draws column strips of tiles $F8/$8C and ground rows at $31E4/$3204 (tiles $8A, $9A).

s0CBBB9.name: Screen image: cutscene 6 background
summary: ImagePointers entry 68, used by cutscene 6 (Wendy). Same layout as the other cutscene backgrounds: clear $3000+, rows of tile $F8, small patches, ground rows at $31E4/$3204.

s0CBD02.name: Screen image: cutscene 1, 2 and 5 background

s0CC94E.name: Cutscene main entry and text timer
summary: CODE_0CC94E: [$1443] counts down; every 32 frames it queues ImagePointers entry 11 + (cutscene-1)*8 + ([$1443] >> 5) in [$12], the next of the 8 text lines ([$13C6] = cutscene 1-7).
CODE_0CC97E (JSL from the cutscene game mode, $009529): runs the text timer, draws the decoration sprites, then CODE_0CC98C counts down [$144D] every 4th frame,
updates Mario's sprite (CODE_0CD803) and jumps to the handler for cutscene [$13C6] through the table at $0CC9A5.

Ptrs0CC9A5.name: Pointer table: cutscene handlers; cutscene 1
summary: Seven handlers indexed by [$13C6]-1 (the castle 1-7 Koopaling cutscenes, 8 = credits is handled elsewhere).
CODE_0CC9B3 (cutscene 1, Iggy): draws sprite slot 0, updates the object at [$0B51], then runs state [$1442] from the table below.

Ptrs0CC9C0.name: Pointer table: cutscene 1 states; cutscene 2
summary: Cutscene 1 state routines (6). Then CODE_0CC9CC (cutscene 2, Morton): updates the object at [$0B51] and runs state [$1442] from the next table.

Ptrs0CC9D6.name: Pointer table: cutscene 2 states; cutscene 5
summary: Cutscene 2 state routines (5). Then CODE_0CC9E0 (cutscene 5, Roy): sprite slot 0, object at [$0B51], CODE_0CD4F8, then state [$1442].

Ptrs0CC9F0.name: Pointer table: cutscene 5 states; cutscene 4
summary: Cutscene 5 state routines (10). Then CODE_0CCA04 (cutscene 4, Ludwig): sprite slot 0; state 0 sets [$1445] = 4; state 7 also runs CODE_0CCF49; then state [$1442].

Ptrs0CCA1F.name: Pointer table: cutscene 4 states; cutscene 3
summary: Cutscene 4 state routines (8). Then CODE_0CCA2F (cutscene 3, Lemmy): CODE_0CD65B, object at [$0B51], CODE_0CD3A6 (except in state 3), CODE_0CD3F4, then state [$1442].

Ptrs0CCA49.name: Pointer table: cutscene 3 states; cutscene 6
summary: Cutscene 3 state routines (4). Then CODE_0CCA51 (cutscene 6, Wendy): CODE_0CD6EC, draws the object tile $E6 at (B0, [$0B51]) when [$1444] is set, then state [$1442].

Ptrs0CCA6E.name: Pointer table: cutscene 6 states; cutscene 7
summary: Cutscene 6 state routines (2). Then CODE_0CCA72 (cutscene 7, Larry): just runs state [$1442] from the next table.

Ptrs0CCA79.name: Pointer table: cutscene 7 states; sprite helpers
summary: Cutscene 7 state routines (5), then shared sprite helpers:
CODE_0CCA8F draws 3 decoration sprites from DATA_0CCA83 (X, Y, tile, properties) in OAM slots 120-122 when [$144A] is set;
CODE_0CCACE controls the object at [$0B51]/[$1444] (draws tile $E6 via CODE_0CCAFD); CODE_0CCB1C is state 0 of cutscenes 1, 4 and 5 (row of sprites);
CODE_0CCB5B draws the 16x16 sprite in OAM slot 0 at (80, 103) with tile $E0 ($E2 when [$143E] is non-zero).

s0CCB80.name: Draw cutscene sprite row and 2x2 block
summary: CODE_0CCB80: draws a row of 5 sprites (tile $E4, 16 pixels apart, y = $67) from X = $60 (or [$0B50] when [$143E] is non-zero), skipping any at X >= $B0,
plus, when [$143E] is non-zero, a small animated sprite (tile $85/$95 by [$1440]) at X = [$0B50]-8, y = $6F; when it passes X = $B0 the cutscene state advances.
CODE_0CCBFA: draws a 2x2 block of sprites from DATA_0CCB7C at (A8, 5F), 8 pixels apart, starting at OAM slot 1 ($0380 + 4); CODE_0CCBFC enters with another slot offset in X.

s0CCC51.name: Cutscene state: backdrop color flash
summary: Each frame the backdrop color mirror $0701 alternates between $7393 and $7FFF (white) every 2 frames, while [$1441] counts down.
A 3x2 sprite block is animated with the frame durations in DATA_0CCC49 and drawn by CODE_0CCCB6, plus the 2x2 block at OAM offset $1C.
When the timer runs out the cutscene objects are cleared, the backdrop color is restored from the Palettes? table using CutsceneBgColor, and the state advances.

s0CCC9F.name: Tile table: 3x2 sprite frames
summary: Tiles for CODE_0CCCB6's 3x2 block of 16x16 sprites (6 bytes per frame, 0 = no sprite); selected by DATA_0CCCB1.

lines.0CAE3F: / Copy the extra image onto the end of the buffer, word by word, up to a $FFFF word

lines.0CAE4D: Window HDMA table 1 ($04A0): scanline count of entry 2
